joints.name: lid

insert.source: McMaster-Carr, Heat-Set Threaded Inserts for Plastic, product page 94459A130 (https://www.mcmaster.com/94459A130/), its specification table read with cadagent.mechanical.mcmaster on 2026-10-27; knurl diameter 4.7 mm from bd_warehouse's McMaster-Carr column s (vendored at e6ae6e7)

material.name: Bambu PETG Basic
material.status: derived from the datasheet; a hypothesis until a printed coupon is measured

clamp.why: recessed below the joint face, the insert is pulled towards the head until the gap closes: the whole preload goes into the knurl, pulling the insert out of the boss
clamp.instead: press the insert in flush (the clamped part then bears on it), or from the far side against a shoulder, or put a compression limiter or a flanged insert in the clamp path; otherwise keep the torque under the pull-out limit

capacity.confidence: low: 3 results from two groups, SPIROL's two M6 results read off a bar chart and CNC Kitchen's M3 (3 samples, the insert's length assumed)
notes: push-out: no published test; the pull-out model is taken as is (low confidence)
lying: no published number; Kastner 2023 found inserts along Z stronger and more predictable

why: the maker's hole is 4 mm; a printed hole comes out about 0.25 mm small, so CAD takes 0.2 mm more (CNC Kitchen 2026: 0.2-0.3 mm for small inserts)
straight, not tapered, and no chamfer (CNC Kitchen tips; SPIROL: a straight hole tapers at most 1 degree included)
blind: 5.3 mm deep, the deepest of the makers' rules, so the melt the insert pushes down has somewhere to go
wall at least 1.6 mm round the hole (CNC Kitchen poster; ruthex)
outside at least 1.5 x the knurl diameter, full performance from 2 x (SPIROL's 3D-printing paper; PEM: boss 2 x the insert diameter)
print the boss solid: 7 perimeters out to its outside, at least as many as the metric size (SPIROL); pull-out rose about 2.5 x from 30 % to 70 % infill (Kastner 2023)
no maker gives an edge distance: keep at least the wall to any free face

preload_kept.basis: plastic in the clamp path (the clamped plastic): it relaxes

on_plastic.text: the ISO 4762 socket head (5.07 mm on a 3.4 mm hole: 11.11 mm^2); the fillet under the head (up to 3.6 mm) is wider than the hole, so it rides on the hole's edge: chamfer it to at least 3.6 mm across

install.temperature: iron about 245 degC (CNC Kitchen tips: 10-20 degC over the print temperature)
install.how: melt it in to about 90 % of its depth with the tip, then press it flush with a flat tool and hold it while it sets (CNC Kitchen tips); heat installation needs little force, generally under 220 N (SPIROL's inserts guide, p. 18); flush, or proud by no more than 0.13 mm (PEM; SPIROL): never below the face, where the screw jacks it out

checks.detail: in CAD; the maker's hole plus 0.2-0.3 mm prints to size (CNC Kitchen 2026)
deep enough for the melt below the insert (the makers' rules)
1.40 mm above the hole's floor; 3.80 of the insert's 4.3 mm of thread engaged
the makers' full-performance boss (2 x the knurl, SPIROL), more than the about 1.5 x the tests that set the low end printed

recessed below the joint face, the insert is pulled towards the head until the gap closes: the whole preload goes into the knurl, pulling the insert out of the boss; instead: press the insert in flush (the clamped part then bears on it), or from the far side against a shoulder, or put a compression limiter or a flanged insert in the clamp path; otherwise keep the torque under the pull-out limit
the most is 0.143 N m, set by jack out

the preload and the separating load on the 3.80 mm of the insert's thread the screw engages, against the force that strips it (2242 N: the ISO 68 internal shear area at brass's shear yield, 0.577 x 124 MPa, the softest temper) / 2
the separating load plus the preload (jack-out) against the low pull-out 563 N / 2

the preload on the plastic under the ISO 4762 socket head (5.07 mm on a 3.4 mm hole: 11.11 mm^2); the fillet under the head (up to 3.6 mm) is wider than the hole, so it rides on the hole's edge: chamfer it to at least 3.6 mm across (MPa) against its compressive strength / 2 (printed PETG's measured compressive strength, Amza 2021); a washer under the head spreads it

the clamped plastic relaxes and takes the preload with it: a printed joint kept 0.885 of its untightening torque after 7 days (Amza 2021); moulded polycarbonate keeps 0.59-0.67 over 1-6 years (Covestro); no long-term printed figure was found. A compression limiter keeps the clamp in metal

limits: the strengths are a shear model calibrated to published pull-out tests of M3 x 5.7 and M6 x 12.7 inserts in printed PLA and PETG; other sizes scale by the knurl's area, but SPIROL's M6 results sit below the M3 ones (their c is lower), so the low end, which the checks use, comes from the larger insert; other families take the lowest fit: a starting point to test (coupon_plan), not a rating
torque-out comes from pull-out through the ratio r = 2 T / (F D) the published tests give (printed and moulded); its low end is taken
push-out has no published test, and an insert lying in the layer plane has no published number: both are flagged, not modelled
static, short-term, room temperature: a held load creeps; PLA inserts kept 26-55 % of their pull-out after a year of natural ageing (Materials 2025)

the boss is printed as the tests printed it: 1.5 x wall thickness, 5 wall loops, at 55 % infill (SPIROL), a 1.3-1.9 mm solid sleeve in 40 % infill, 1.5-1.75 x the knurl (Laszlo 2026), or solid (CNC Kitchen); a 2 x boss, the makers' full performance, is stronger than the tests behind the low end; fewer walls or sparser infill hold less (SPIROL's Figure 8: one wall loop at 15 % infill held about a quarter of eleven; Kastner 2023: 30 to 70 % infill raised pull-out about 2.5 x)
the insert's end takes the whole clamp where the clamped part or a limiter bears on it, brass being far stiffer than the boss round it, so its face is held to the softest temper's yield (124 MPa)
a printed clamped part on a flush insert is taken to carry the whole clamp on the insert's ring, the cautious side: once it yields the boss face takes some, which nothing here sizes
a far-side insert is taken as pressed onto the shoulder in front of it
a size outside the fitted ones (M3 x 5.7, M6 x 12.7) takes the fit as it is: larger ones are flagged, as the published results fall with size
preload relaxation: printed PLA was measured for an hour and printed joints for a week; the long-term figure is moulded polycarbonate's, and PLA, nearer its glass transition, will keep less
CAD and closed forms do not prove a joint holds: print the coupons and measure
